note: The `chart` layer is THE CONTINUOUS OBJECT and the film's only explanation. A North Atlantic chart on the scene clock: coastlines and the 20-degree graticule fade up over New York, the great-circle JFK->CDG draws on while the counter reads 3,635 mi (so the arc IS the distance, not a caption for it), the aircraft then flies that arc laying a solid track behind it, and the dawn line sweeps WEST across the map because the terminator moves west and an eastbound redeye flies into it. That sweep is the hook's 'one night in between', shown. Geometry is one linear lon/lat mapping, x = 60 + (lon + 80) * 15.682 and y = 520 - (lat - 36) * 17.143, so every coast vertex and both airports sit where they really are; the arc is the quadratic through the true great-circle midpoint near 36W 51.5N. It carries acrossBeats, so it survives all four cuts and changes across each one, while the type is demoted to a band above it.

layers.text: Two cities. One night in between.
one arc, drawn across five cuts

layers.text: Then six hours of nothing to look at.
Landed. Gate K42, five minutes early.
One route. It crossed every cut.
